'''Joel W. Martin''' (born 1955) is an American [[Marine biology|marine biologist]] and invertebrate zoologist who is currently Chief of the Division of Invertebrate Studies and Curator of Crustacea at the [[Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County]] (NHMLAC).<ref name="nhmlac">{{cite web
|url=http://crustacea.nhm.org/people/martin
|title=Crustacea Section, Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County
|accessdate=11 December 2010
|archive-date=30 May 2014
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140530183421/http://crustacea.nhm.org/people/martin/
|url-status=dead
}}</ref>  His main area of research is the [[morphology (biology)|morphology]] and [[systematics]] of marine [[Decapoda|decapod]] [[crustacean]]s ([[crab]]s, [[shrimp]]s, [[lobster]]s and their relatives).{{citation needed|date=December 2010}}

Martin received a doctorate from the [[Florida State University]] in 1986.<ref name="nhmlac" /> He has published more than 100 scientific articles and books mainly on morphology, [[natural history]], [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]], and evolutionary relationships of both [[Decapoda|decapod]]s  and of [[Branchiopoda|branchiopods]] of [[ephemeral pool]]s. His work also includes studies on the animals inhabiting deep-sea [[hydrothermal vent]]s and [[cold seep]]s. He is perhaps best known for his 2001 publication of an updated classification of recent crustaceans.<ref>
{{cite journal
|last1=Martin
|first1= Joel W.
|first2=George E.
|last2=Davis
|date=1 December 2001
|url=http://www.vliz.be/imisdocs/publications/121258.pdf
|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110426090556/http://www.vliz.be/imisdocs/publications/121258.pdf
|url-status = dead
|archive-date = 26 April 2011
|title=An Updated Classification of the Recent Crustacea
|publisher=Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County
|series=Science Series No. 39.
|pages=124
}}</ref>
In addition to his research on [[marine invertebrates]], he has been active on communicating questions of [[global biodiversity]] and on the history and interaction of science and religious faith.<ref>{{cite book
|last1=Martin
|first1= Joel W.
|year=2010
|title=The Prism and the Rainbow: A Christian Explains Why Evolution Is Not a Threat
|publisher=Johns Hopkins University Press
|pages=192
|isbn=9780801894787
}}</ref>
